subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: What is the supported lifecycle for cron quarantine recovery archives after overflow: explicit operator cleanup, a maintainer-approved automatic retention limit, or no archive-and-continue recovery?
rationale: This determines whether potentially useful recovery data may be removed automatically and whether repeated recovery can consume unlimited disk; the code cannot safely infer the product retention policy.

options.title: Add explicit Doctor cleanup
options.body: Keep recovery archives by default, surface their count and size through Doctor, and make deletion an explicit operator action.

options.title: Approve bounded automatic retention
options.body: Retain a fixed number or age window of archives and document that oldest recovery data is deleted automatically.

options.title: Avoid persistent archives
options.body: Reject saturated quarantine writes instead of archiving and continuing, preserving a strict bounded-disk behavior at the cost of recovery continuity.

recommendation.title: Add explicit Doctor cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep recovery archives by default, surface their count and size through Doctor, and make deletion an explicit operator action.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main file ownership could not be established from the available provenance, so a cron/storage owner should make the retention decision.
